target.manifest_sha256_note: SHA-256 of the checked-in NVFP4 manifest itself. Unlike the retired 4-bit placeholder this manifest is fully populated and byte-verified (13 entries) and is the SAME manifest the live serial track uses, so the DFlash track reuses the already-provisioned reference checkpoint cache.
target.expected_source_bytes_note: Sum of the 13 pinned entries in fixtures/reference_laguna_xs_2_1_nvfp4_mlx.sha256 (NVFP4 group-16 reference checkpoint).
target.quantization_note: MLX affine 4-bit group-64 with per-layer exceptions: the MoE router gate projections (language_model.model.layers.{1..39}.mlp.gate.proj) are affine 8-bit group-64 per the runtime checkpoint config.json.

quantization.note: Matches the live serial track's reference checkpoint so DFlash speedups stay comparable to serial-track timings. Supersedes the retired track's mlx-community 4-bit affine group-64 target.

assistant.manifest_sha256_note: TODO(operator): SHA-256 of the manifest file itself, pinned after the manifest is regenerated on m5-bench (the checked-in manifest is a placeholder header only).
assistant.expected_total_bytes_note: The upstream BF16 model.safetensors payload at revision 5c36361 per Hugging Face LFS metadata (config.json adds 963 bytes). The draft is provisioned as BF16 and converted to MLX affine 4-bit (group size 64) at setup. TODO(operator): confirm on m5-bench when the manifest is regenerated.
assistant.maximum_total_bytes_note: 1 GiB budget: headroom over the 924135848-byte BF16 draft download that setup converts to MLX 4-bit.
assistant.quantization_note: The pinned upstream draft ships BF16 (torch_dtype bfloat16); setup-mtp.sh converts it to MLX affine 4-bit (group size 64) on-box. The bits/group fields describe the runtime-converted form.

protocol.name: trusted_dflash_block_v1
protocol.maximum_block_size_note: Raised from 4 (Gemma-MTP assistant era) to 16: the DFlash draft model's config block_size is 16 and it drafts a whole masked block in one forward. Measured on M5 (dev-repo binary, 2026-07-30): peak decode speedup at K=8 (1.60x), K=16 slightly lower (1.53x); K remains a runtime choice bounded by this maximum.

reference_baseline._note: The paired serial K=1 baseline, floor calibration, and hidden goldens for Laguna XS 2.1 must be established on m5-bench before this flips to established/publication_allowed=true (go-live runbook steps B-C).

proposed_scoring.aggregation: ratio_of_means: mean(serial seconds/token across accepted pairs) / mean(dflash seconds/token across accepted pairs)
proposed_scoring.paired_serial_reference: trusted serial K=1 target decode (probe path) over the same golden, same session, same thermal gate, same box
proposed_scoring.denominator_authority: trusted parent wall time divided by the parent-configured decode total
proposed_scoring.component_floor: aggregate dflash_decode_speedup >= 1.0 (floor applies to the ratio-of-means aggregate, not per pair)
proposed_scoring.token_fidelity_gate: PENDING SPEC (supersedes the Gemma-MTP bit_exact_gate). The MTP-era criterion -- every returned token must exactly match the trusted SEQUENTIAL oracle -- is empirically unachievable for DFlash on Laguna NVFP4: the target's own block-shaped forward diverges from K sequential forwards at near-tie argmax positions with NO drafter involved (measured on M5 2026-07-30: 14/14 divergences were target block-vs-sequential; max sequential-logit gap 0.625; 12/14 were sequential rank 2, one rank 3, one rank 5 in a flat distribution). The replacement criterion is trusted sequential re-verification with a bounded near-tie budget; exact values are being specified separately and MUST be written here before official_scoring_enabled can flip to true.
proposed_scoring.stall_guardrail: a run whose max block latency exceeds 4x its p50 block latency is rejected as measurement-invalid with one gated retry
proposed_scoring.prefill_component: none; seed prefill is charged inside the decode measurement
proposed_scoring.leaderboard: separate laguna-xs-2.1-dflash-v1 namespace, never mixed with the serial track
proposed_scoring.measurement_protocol: minimum three accepted thermal-gated pairs per session (target four) with alternating order; single-pair scores are not publishable
